paper.title: Algorithm 885: Computing the logarithm of the normal distribution

field: numerics (special functions, log of the normal tail)
stack: C (TOMS 885, lnnorm.c with the authors' driver main.c and Doc/makefile)

claim.text: -lnnorm(-5.0) computed by the authors' C/lnnorm.c, against the Sheppard (1939) Table IV row x = 5.0 in the shipped C/sheppard.txt: 15.0649983939887257, absolute tolerance 1.5e-8

attempt: Reproduced with a patched build. The authors' Doc/makefile does not link on this host as documented (the -lm precedes the objects; the default --as-needed linker rejects it, 'undefined reference to log'; original attempt failed, logged). The same makefile, unchanged, is run with one linker flag, CFLAGS='-Wl,--no-as-needed -lm'; no source file or makefile line is edited, and the build is proven build-only by three manifests (verify_sources record). The authors' driver main prints only maxima and means over the table, not the single claimed value, so a probe (impl/probe_lnnorm.c, written from the claim text) calls the authors' lnnorm() at x = -5.0 and prints -lnnorm(-5.0) with 17 significant digits. Two clean passes give 15.064998393988725 both times; |ours - paper| is zero at the printed precision, inside tol_abs 1.5e-8. The driver's whole-table output is kept as evidence (driver-stdout). The paper (ACM DL) was not read; the claim rests on the shipped table. Replay (G5) not yet run.

original_attempt.reason: link error: the makefile places -lm before the objects; the default --as-needed linker rejects it (undefined reference to log, exp, erf, ...)
